text: Snow Rings are Mechanical collectibles in . They can be found in the Gormott Province by Salvaging at any Gormott Salvage Point. In the , Snow Rings can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.
Speck Butchers is a shop in . It is run by Lucida and can be found in Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago. It is specialized in Meats.
The Speck Deeds are Store Deeds in . They can be purchased from Speck Butchers in Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Snowbaby Potato Salads are Veggie Pouch items in . They can be purchased at Corcaja Greengrocers in Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago. They are one of Nia's favorite Pouch Items in her Blade form. Four need to be used to unlock Nia's Level 3 "Water Mastery" Field Skill. They can also be purchased for 2,520 G from the Pouch Item Emporium in the Land of Challenge after collecting the Nopon Invitation, Pt. 2 on Version 1.5.2 or later.

Spike Urchons (Japanese: , Supaiku Unin) are enemies in . They are members of the Urchon family, and can be found at level 35-37 in the Fonsa Myma Waters in the Stomach area of the Kingdom of Uraya. Three of them must be defeated during the quest Sniff out the Spy.
Sparda Ignas (Japanese: , Supāda Igūna) are enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 48 - 53 at the Bastion of Varrac on the Central Plain of Temperantia.
Snowdol Bunnits (Japanese: , Yūkido Banitto) are enemies in . They are members of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 36-40 at Litharia Snowfield on the Upper Level of the Kingdom of Tantal.

Spinel Urchons (Japanese: , Supineru Unin) are enemies in . They are members of the Urchon family, and can be found at level 40-42 at the Sacred Ice Caverns on the Upper Level of the Kingdom of Tantal.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Spiked Pauldrons (Japanese: , Supaiku Shorudā) are accessories in and . They increase damage dealt by inflicting Smash by up to 60%. The Hero Pauldrons, Jet Pauldrons, and Consul Pauldrons accessories offer stronger instances of this equipment's effect.
Soap Corals are Ore collectibles in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Uraya.
Soapberry Boxes are Tree collectibles in . They can be found in the Land of Morytha, in particular from the Collection Point located north of the Womb Hollow.

Space Cardoons are Flower collectibles in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Uraya, in particular from the Collection Point at Yurna the Elderwood. In the , Space Cardoons can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo. Two of them are needed to craft a Rizzente Mantle.

Spark Cucumbers are Vegetable collectibles in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Uraya, specifically at the Collection Point northeast of Yurna the Elderwood. One can be used to prepare a ration needed for the quest The Supply Situation.
Speckled Whalefishes are Fish collectibles in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Uraya, in particular from the Collection Point located northeast of Yurna the Elderwood.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Soldier Rings (Japanese: , Sorujā Ringu) are accessories in and . They extend the duration of the Launch reaction by up to 17% (0.85 seconds). This effect will only apply when the wearer inflicts the reaction. The Berserk Ring, Tyrant Ring and Goliath Ring accessories offer stronger instances of this equipment's effect.
Soul Suckers are Treasure items in . They can be obtained through Salvaging at Jubilee Gate on the Cliffs of Morytha.
Sore Worms are Insect collectibles in . They can be found in the Land of Morytha.

Sphere Chips are Core Chips in and . They can be dropped by a variety of enemies, primarily in Temperantia and the Cliffs of Morytha, and bought from Bamboo Sword Smithy. In , they can be dropped by Beatific Ophelia or rewarded upon completion of What Goes Around. Sphere Chips share their appearance with Polygon Chips, Cube Chips, and Spiral Chips. __TOC__

Spinel Chips are Core Chips in and . In , they can be purchased at the Proplater Blacksmiths shop in the Kingdom of Uraya, found in a Treasure Trove at the Stone Gate Ruins in Uraya, and dropped by a variety of enemies primarily in Uraya. In , they are acquired as quest rewards and dropped by two enemies. Spinel Chips share their appearance with Amethyst Chips, Fluorite Chips and Turquoise Chips. __TOC__

Spiral Chips are Core Chips in . They can be obtained in the Kingdom of Tantal. All weapons forged with a Spiral Chip deal 50% more damage against aquatic organisms. They can only be dropped by the high level enemies Armored Brennan, Rambl Marrins, Rampaging Sauros (quest-exclusive), and Relentless Arduran. They are also given as a quest reward for A Secret Cure. Spiral Chips share their appearance with Polygon Chips, Sphere Chips, and Cube Chips. __TOC__

Spanner Bunnits (Japanese: , Supāna Banitto) are enemies in . They are members of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 27-29 in the pipe south of the Thermal Exhaust Fork in the Empire of Mor Ardain. Five of them must be defeated to unlock KOS-MOS' level 2 "Light Mastery" and Vale's level 3 Blood Altar.
Speed Runners (Japanese: , Supīdo Rannā) are enemies in . They are members of the Rapchor family, and can be found at level 27-29 at the Jelidorend Highlands in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Solala is an NPC in . Solala is a Nopon who can be found at Fonsa Myma Port in the Kingdom of Uraya during Fame and Family, and at Rumbletum Canteen in the Argentum Trade Guild after completing the quest. He is Falala's son.

|-|Aux Core = |-|Skill RAM/Upgrade = Specials Lv 1 Plus (Japanese: , Hissatsuwaza Lv1 Kyōka) is an Aux Core or a Skill RAM/Upgrade in and . It increases the damage dealt by Level 1 Specials by up to 70%. The Skill RAM/Upgrade variants can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ as an Aux Core equivalent. __TOC__

|-|Aux Core = |-|Skill RAM/Upgrade = Specials Lv 2 Plus (Japanese: , Hissatsuwaza Lv2 Kyōka) is an Aux Core or a Skill RAM/Upgrade in and . It increases the damage dealt by Level 2 Specials by up to 70%. The Skill RAM/Upgrade variants can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ as an Aux Core equivalent. __TOC__

|-|Aux Core = |-|Skill RAM/Upgrade = Specials Lv 3 Plus (Japanese: , Hissatsuwaza Lv3 Kyōka) is an Aux Core or a Skill RAM/Upgrade in and . It increases the damage dealt by Level 3 Specials by up to 70%. The Skill RAM/Upgrade variants can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ as an Aux Core equivalent. __TOC__

|-|Aux Core = |-|Skill RAM/Upgrade = Specials Lv 4 Plus (Japanese: , Hissatsuwaza Lv4 Kyōka) is an Aux Core or a Skill RAM/Upgrade in and . It increases the damage dealt by Level 4 Specials by up to 70%. The Skill RAM/Upgrade variants can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ as an Aux Core equivalent. __TOC__

|-|Aux Core = |-|Skill RAM/Upgrade = Spike Defense (Japanese: , Supaiku Bōgyo) is an Aux Core or a Skill RAM/Upgrade in and . It lowers incoming spike damage by up to 100%, allowing for spike damage to be reduced down to 1 per hit. The Skill RAM/Upgrade variants can be used to customize Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ as an Aux Core equivalent. __TOC__

The Sparkly Snow Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Farming Tech. It enables the purchase of Sparkly Snow Perfumes from the Cosmetipolitan shop at Torigoth in the Gormott Province.

The Snowflake Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Farming Tech. It enables the purchase of Snowflake Scarves from the Neuromin Textiles shop at Torigoth in the Gormott Province.

The Snowbaby Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Sinking Storehouse?. It enables the purchase of Snowbaby Potato Salad from the Corcaja Greengrocers shop at Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Special Concert (Japanese: , Supesharukonsāto) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula obtains 4,000 fans. It increases Ursula's fanbase by a large amount. The time required to complete this mission is 40 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 10 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Water Mastery" and "Electric Mastery" Field Skills.

Sparkly Costumes (Japanese: , Kirakira Ishō) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula's Vocals, Looks and Soul reach Level 3. It increases Ursula's fanbase by a significant amount. The time required to complete this mission is 20 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 5 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Wind Mastery", "Fire Mastery" and "Weaving" Field Skills.

Song Selection is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula's Vocals, Looks and Soul reach Level 5. The time required to complete this mission is 20 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 5 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Electric Mastery", "Earth Mastery" and "Beguiling Charms" Field Skills. It increases Ursula's fanbase by a significant amount. This mission will become unobtainable if not unlocked before the end of the quest.

Soul Lesson 1 (Japanese: , Souru Ressun 1) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul. The time required to complete this mission is 10 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 2 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Expeditionist" and "Wind Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards Soul Stamps that are necessary to level up Ursula's Soul Level. It also slightly increases Ursula's fanbase the first time it is cleared.

Soul Lesson 2 (Japanese: , Souru Ressun 2) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula's Soul reaches Level 2. The time required to complete this mission is 10 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 2 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Expeditionist" and "Ice Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards Soul Stamps that are necessary to level up Ursula's Soul Level. It also slightly increases Ursula's fanbase the first time it is cleared.

Soul Lesson 3 (Japanese: , Souru Ressun 3) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula's Soul reaches Level 4. The time required to complete this mission is 10 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 2 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Expeditionist" and "Earth Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards Soul Stamps that are necessary to level up Ursula's Soul Level. It also slightly increases Ursula's fanbase the first time it is cleared.

Soul Lesson 4 (Japanese: , Souru Ressun 4) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula's Soul reaches Level 6. The time required to complete this mission is 10 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 2 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Expeditionist" and "Light Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards Soul Stamps that are necessary to level up Ursula's Soul Level. It also slightly increases Ursula's fanbase the first time it is cleared. This mission will become unobtainable if not unlocked before the end of the quest.

Soul Lesson 5 (Japanese: , Souru Ressun 5) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula's Soul reaches Level 8. The time required to complete this mission is 10 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 2 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Expeditionist", "Wind Mastery" and "Ice Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards Soul Stamps that are necessary to level up Ursula's Soul Level. It also slightly increases Ursula's fanbase the first time it is cleared. This mission will become unobtainable if not unlocked before the end of the quest.
Souvenirs from Morytha is a quest in . It can be received from Dibidi at the Cliffs of Morytha's Inlet.

Sourlip Drinks are Drink Pouch items in . They can be prepared from a recipe requiring one Cranberry Bell and nine Panda Pansies at Rumbletum Canteen in the Argentum Trade Guild during the quest Fame and Family.
The Special Blade Medicine is a Key Item in . It is received from Smaia at the Admar Storage Zone in the Empire of Mor Ardain, during the quest A Secret Cure.
Sorbl Krabbles (Japanese: , Sābaru Kuraibu) are enemies in . They are members of the Krabble family, and can be found at level 44-48 at the Morytha Falls on the Cliffs of Morytha after Salvaging.
Sophonea is an NPC in . She is a Tantalese who can be found at the Library Philosofia in the Kingdom of Tantal. She offers the Merc Mission New Book.
Sokoko is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who can be found in the Leftherian Archipelago. He offers the Quest At Wit's End.

Sparkling Snowglobes are Art Pouch items in . They can be made by Dahlia using her "Icecraft Lv.2" field skill at the Dahlia's Icecraft table in Argentum's Goldmouth Warehouse. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of MOMO in her Real Mode.
Soul Stamps are Key Items in . They can be obtained as rewards for completing the Merc Missions Soul Lessons 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 during the quest Bearing Her Soul.
The Solemn Statue is a Key Item in . It is accidentally stolen by Boreas during the Blade Quest Hero of the Nopon, from Gianluca the sculptor. It must subsequently be returned to him.
Sornathea is an NPC in . She is a Tantalese who can be found in the Residential Area of Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal. She is the mother of Martal and is involved during the Quest Eternal Spirit.
Sosoma is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who can be found on Quattor Street in the Indoline Praetorium. He runs the shop Aquarius Salvaging.

Spektr Aligos are Challenge Battle Enemies in . They are members of the Aligo family, and can be found at level 106 summoned by Cloud Sea King Ken during Cloud King's Revenge, a Challenge Battle, available as downloadable content from the Challenge Battle Mode Pack of the Expansion Pass. This enemy drops no items.

Spektr Crustips are Challenge Battle Enemies in . They are members of the Crustip family, and can be found at level 102 summoned by Cloud Sea King Ken during the Challenge Battle Cloud King's Revenge. This enemy drops no items.

Spektr Urchons are Challenge Battle Enemies in . They are members of the Urchon family, and can be found at level 110 summoned by Cloud Sea King Ken during the Challenge Battle Cloud King's Revenge. This enemy drops no items.
Soothing Breeze (Japanese: , Burīzuhīru, Lit. "Breeze Heal") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Nia's arts when wielding Knives. This art recycles Nia's Healing Halo.

So-Called Best Artisan is a DLC Shop in . It is run by Barhanen and can be found southeast from Elmos Square within Theosoir, in the Kingdom of Tantal, during and after completing the DLC Quest Artisanal Accessories available as downloadable content, the New Quests Pack 4 of the Expansion Pass. To access this shop, two "Airflow" Field Skill checks need to be cleared in order to climb a large structure, requiring "Wind Mastery" Lv.3, "Earth Mastery" Lv.7 and "Leaping" Lv.4.
Sovereign Approach (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when wielding an Uchigatana.
Soothing Twilight (Japanese: , Towairaitohīru, Lit. "Twilight Heal") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Nia's arts when wielding Dual Swords.
Spessia (Sperantia, "Hope", in the Japanese dub) is a location seen during cutscenes in both and . It is never an explorable location in either game, but important story events transpire there.
Sorolle Armus (Japanese: , Sororu Aruma) are minor enemies in . They are members of the Armu family and can be found at level 11 - 17 on Wrackham Moor in the Aletta Region of the Kingdom of Torna.

Sowl Feris (Japanese: , Souru Ferisu) are minor enemies in . They can be found in the Aletta Region of the Kingdom of Torna, on Wrackham Moor. They drop Feris Beastmeat which is required for the Main Quest Feeding an Army.
Soothing Talismans are Talisman items in . They can be created by Haze at Campsites.
Spicy Scorpion Cookies are Dessert items in . They can be created by Mythra at Campsites.
Spiral Mistletoes are Tree collectible items in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Torna.
Sour Avocados are Vegetable collectible items in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Torna.
Speckled Monarchs are Insect collectible items in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Torna.

Somelia Nests (Japanese: , Someiyu Nesuto) are minor enemies in . They are members of the Nest family and can be found at level 21 - 24 on Olnard's Trail and Wrackham Moor in the Aletta Region of the Kingdom of Torna.

Sordis Rhoguls (Japanese: , Sōdisu Rōguru) are minor enemies in . They are members of the Rhogul family and can be found at level 19 - 24 on Wrackham Moor and in the Tirkin Cliff Colony in the Aletta Region of the Kingdom of Torna.

Sorrel is an NPC in . She is a Tornan chef who can be found near Auresco, Main Gate in the Kingdom of Torna; her cooking has suffered due to her grief about the war, but Maulton is trying to help her get back into her work. She gives the quest Great Tornan Cook-Off, and her Community is gained alongside Maulton's upon its completion.
Spindle Step (Japanese: ) is one of Lora's Rear Guard Arts in .
Spinning Wheel (Japanese: ) is one of Lora's Vanguard Arts in . When used, Lora spins her whip around to attack enemies close to her.
Spectral Halo (Japanese: , Supekutoramuheirō, Lit. "Spectrum Halo") is one of Mythra's Rear Guard Arts in .

Spillit Urchons (Japanese: , Supiritto Unin) are minor enemies in . They are members of the Urchon family and can be found at level 60 in the Great Crater of Feltley Village in the Lasaria Region of the Kingdom of Torna when summoned, eight at a time, by the Golden Monster Sentinel Carpathia. They resemble the Sentinel Carpathia exactly other than their size, which is far smaller. This enemy drops no items.

Sorgus Tirkins (Japanese: , Soukisu Tākin) are quest exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Tirkin family, and can be found at level 30 on Golden Twin Mesa in the Kingdom of Torna during the quest Armus Gone Astray alongside two Vanadium Tirkin. As with all quest exclusive enemies in , they drop no items, only gold.

Solthas is a High Entia in . He can be found at Companions' Cape on the Bionis' Shoulder during the day. During the quest Steady on, Grandad!, he can be found in Nerthis Necropolis, after which he returns to Companions' Cape.

Sparkle Stones are five Key Items in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are found among the rocks near the lake where Junks landed, and are required for Brace for Friendship given by Angela.
Soloist's Boosters are Mechonis leg armour in . They can be bought at shops for 24,000 G.
Soloist's Drones are Mechonis Drones in . They can be bought at shops for 30,000 G.
Soloist's Arms are Mechonis arms in . They can be bought at shops for 13,500 G.
Soloist's Frames are Mechonis frame in . They can be bought at shops for 25,500 G.
Soloist's Goggles are Mechonis goggles in . They can be bought at shops for 18,000 G

Soulfire (Japanese: , Shiranui) is Hugo and Brighid's Level IV Blade Special in . It is unlocked once the party sets off for Auresco. If Soulfire is activated by Hugo, the special's element will be determined by the Arming Sword he has equipped.
Super Sonic Thunderbolt Slash (Japanese: ) abbreviated Sonic Thunderslash, is Pandoria's Level IV Blade Special in .
Soul Burst (Japanese: , Sourubāsuto) is Addam's Level III Special in . As with Addam's other specials, the element of Soul Burst is determined by the Greatsword he has equipped.
Snowflake of Judgment (Japanese: ) is Perun's Level IV Blade Special in .
Snughug Blockers are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are blockers wielded by Nene.
Snughug Blockers C are weapons in . They are blockers wielded by Nene.
Snughug Blockers L are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are blockers wielded by Nene.
Sparres Barr (Japanese: , Supasu Kyūryō) is a Location in , located in the Ribbi Flats.

The Soul Tree (Japanese: , sourutsurī) is a game mechanic in . It unlocks upgrades for the main characters' Ouroboros forms, unlocking and enhancing Arts and Skills innate to their Ouroboros. It is comparable to the Skill Tree in and the Affinity Chart in .
Sonata Saddleback (Japanese: , Sōmei no Oka) is a location in , located east of Colony 9 on Yzana Plains. The Unique Monster Repulsive Deepus can be found here.
Solid Stance (Japanese: , Gādosutansu) is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Heavy Guard class. It becomes a usable Master Art upon achieving Rank 10 with the class.
The Sparkling Pool Camp (Japanese: , Kirakira-ike no Kyūsokuchi) is a Rest Spot in . It is located in High Maktha Wildwood.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Soldier's Headbands are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the Colony Tau Commissary and Old Way Caravan. The legendary variant can be purchased at the Prize X-change Red, or from Ambusher Tirion.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Solid Socks are Accessories in and .

Soaring Virion (Japanese: , Chūten no Vāze) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Rhogul family, and can be found at level 36 near Amoney's Hallows at Great Cotte Falls. The Dangerous Claws Skill can be earned by the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Spartan Fennick (Japanese: , Shungen no Feneku) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Ageshu family, and can be found at level 78 in a poison lake near Gingin's Treehouse in Low Maktha Wildwood. The Ministorm Art can be earned by the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Spectral Rémy (Japanese: , Kakuriyo no Rumī) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Medooz family, and can be found at level 42 on Bannis Path near Headwater Camp at the Great Sword's Base. The Toxic Gas Art can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Spiky Aurelia (Japanese: , Keikyoku no Ōreria) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Antol family, and can be found at level 63 in the Antol Pit in Erythia Sea. The Queenly Pride Skill can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.
The South Sector Passage (Japanese: , Minamikukan Renrakutsūro) is a Location in , located in the Origin Interior.
The South Shell Passage (Japanese: , Nanmen Gaikaku Tsūro) is a Location in , located in the Origin Interior.
So Much More to See is a Standard Quest in . It is received immediately upon the completion of the last quest of Dorin and Bambam's questline.
Sol Piranhax are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Piranhax family, and can be found at level 21-22 in Riez Tarn in Rae-Bel Tableland.
Spheric Rocks are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Keves Castle Region. They can also be produced from the Perimeter Outlet Fabricator after the first step of Colony 0 renovation.
Speculatos (Japanese: , Supekuratosu) are Minor Enemies in . They are Kevesi Levnises, and can be found at level 39-40 in Keves Castle.

Solis Rings are Accessories in and . Only one can be obtained per playthrough, from the Legacy of the Seven container at Demihuman Gutter. It is guarded by King Krawkin and Conqueror Deepwan. In , they can be dropped from Fogdweller Abaasy.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Special Foot Wraps are Accessories in and . The legendary variant can be purchased at the Prize X-change Red. In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Tenebrous Muramasa.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Soft Foot Wraps are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the Cascade Caravan. The legendary variant can be obtained from Massive Georges.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Sonic Sensors are Accessories in and . The Aural Enhance Sensor and Ultra Aural Sensor have weaker versions of this accessory's effect. In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Naberius Invictus.

Sodie Stones are Key Items in . Three can be found near Watchtower No. 1 in the Perimeter Woodland of Li Garte Prison Camp, while seven are received from Hackt. Ten are needed for the quest A Chance Encounter, where they are used to repair Eilis's Levnis.
Snow Pansies are Collectible items in . They can be found in Swordmarch, or via the Fabricator at Perimeter Outlet in the Cadensia Region after the first step of Colony 0 renovation.
Sotorig Quadwings are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Quadwing family, and can be found at level 44-45 at the Great Sword's Base.
Sodorio Camills are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Camill family, and can be found at level 45-51 on Daedal Isle in Erythia Sea.

Spearpoint Thrust (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is one of the arts of the Thaumaturge class. It becomes a usable Master Art upon achieving Rank 10 with the class. The user readies their staff then thrusts it forward.
Soulgaze Headbands are DLC Accessories in . They can be purchased from Prize X-change Red in the Land of Challenge for 6000 Noponstones.
Snowdrift (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is a variant of Way Home that can only be used by Miyabi. She sets up a green sphere of energy and launches it at enemies.

Spinning Bolt is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Diabolical Rindolph while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.
Sonorous Taos are two DLC Quest Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Taos family, and can be found at level 43 at Piento Basin in the Eagus Wilderness during Lapidarist Extraordinaire.
Solid Silver is a Battle Art in . It is one of Masha's arts as a Hero.

Snow Pippitos are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Pippito family, and can be found at level 30 west of Lumos Pillar Remnants on The Ragmos Desolation during Light Snow. They can drop Blessed Pippito Lights.

Soldiers' Paean is a track from , composed by Kenji Hiramatsu. It is track twelve of disc one from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track twelve of disc twelve from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It is a remix of Keves Colony. This song plays in Colony 9 during Chapter 1. It also plays when the soldiers of Colony 9 are tilling the fields during Reasons to Evolve.

Something's Beginning to Move is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track eleven of disc eight from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track eleven of disc nineteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the ending after Z's defeat, as the party decides to restore the worlds of the Bionis and Alrest.
Somebody's Memo is a Key Item in . It is a memo written by Wunwun that is dropped by the Cutpurse Igna during Priority Wunwun.
Special Lecture is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in front of the BLADE Scout Console in the BLADE Concourse, in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles between Neilnail and Cross.
Socol is an NPC in . She is an Ardainian who can be found at Poldis Circle in the Indoline Praetorium.

Soghra is an NPC in . He is an Ardainian who can be found in Hardhaigh Dock, Lv. 2 in the Empire of Mor Ardain during Chapter 7. He must be talked to when the party sets off for the Cliffs of Morytha for the first time.

Steel Cutlasses (Japanese: , Kōtetsu no Katana) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are swords wielded by Dunban, and are not dropped by any enemies. Instead, they can be bought in Satorl Marsh or traded for.

Steel Silks (Japanese: , Kōtetsu no Kenpu) are collectables in . They can be found in Tephra Cave. According to their description, Dunban named them sometime prior to the events of the game and they are soft as silk when wet. Two are required for Colony 6 Reconstruction. In , they can be purchased from the Nopon Archsage in Time Attack for 9,200 Noponstones.

Spotted Volff Hides (Japanese: , Vorufu no Madaragara Kegawa) are rare materials in . They can be dropped by some Volffs on Bionis' Leg or traded for with Elior. According to their description, they are mottled pelts with spots that are well-ventilated. Two are required for Colony 6 Reconstruction. In , they can be purchased in the Time Attack place from the Nopon Archsage for 900 Noponstones.

Squall Elements are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from Bono and Emeraude Nebula. Squall Elements are also available for trade. According to their description, they are wind elements that cause a strong wind to blow when thrown in the air. Two Squall Elements are needed to complete Colony 6 Reconstruction. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 2,600 Noponstones.

Stormy Widardun (Japanese: , Bōfū no Waidāden) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Quadwing family, and can be found at level 25 in a tree, on the ridge west of Zaldania Waterfall in Satorl Marsh during the day. It can drop the Quadwing Bags needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Steel Selua Cells are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Victorious Gross and Wool Selua in the Bionis' Interior. There is one Wool Selua in Pars Sympathica Tower. According to their description, they are normally soft, but they harden instantly at the moment of impact. Three are needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 9,100 Noponstones.

Steel Hauynes (Japanese: , Kōtetsu Auin) are collectables in . They can be found in the Eryth Sea. According to their description, Reyn named them boldly and they are purple items that are both gemstone and steel.
Stormy Belagon (Japanese: , Bōfū no Beruragan) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Kromar family and can be found at level 87 at the Kromar Coast, in Eryth Sea.

Spirit Clematises (Japanese: , Dandekuremachisu) are collectables in . They can be found in Colony 6. According to their description, their petals look a bit intimidating, but they are supremely beautiful and fragrant.

Splish Splashes (Japanese: , Dobadobadobabecho) are collectables in . They can be found in Galahad Fortress and Colony 6. According to their description, Riki was not thinking when he named them and touching them stains someone's hand red.

This quest will expire after the decision to move to Colony 6, and if Imaginations Tempered is completed instead. Spirits Raised (Japanese: , Kimi no Okuru Monogatari) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Arda in the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg. As with all the quests in the Refugee Camp, it will expire after the residents migrate to Colony 6. This quest and Imaginations Tempered are mutually exclusive.

※ After this quest is completed, Tati may offer Musical Genius. Also afterwards, Pipiki may offer Honouring the Nopon Sage. Strange Noises from Below (Japanese: , Chika kara no Bukimina Koe) is a quest in . It can be received from Pipiki in the Central Plaza, west border of the Sacred Altar's pool, in Frontier Village. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.
The Steady Driver (Japanese: , Baransubankā) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn. It can be bought from three shops, but is not dropped by any enemies.
Stealth Rifles (Japanese: , Suterusuraifuru) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Ether rifles wielded by Sharla, and are not dropped by any enemies, but can be bought or traded for.

Spiral Valley (Japanese: , Rasen Tani) is a landmark in . It is located on the upper level of Bionis' Leg. It is where Shulk, Sharla and Reyn find Juju after he runs off to Colony 6. They fight Mechon M71 on top of a large stone slab. Upon defeating this Mechon, Xord comes in and, after a brief battle with the others, he flies away with Juju. After that battle, whenever the party comes to this landmark, a level 90 Unique Monster, the Immovable Gonzalez, guards the entrance, stopping the party from returning to the center. However, a quest later on in Colony 6 allows them to climb up the middle part from the bottom, in Windy Cave.
Steady Helms (Japanese: , Gorudo Herumu) are heavy head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.

The Splintered Path (Japanese: , Kyoshin no Shidō) is a location in . It is located at Colony 6. It is accessed by using a lift at the top of the map, near Watchpoint Junction and the entrance from Bionis' Leg. It is a series of connected paths hanging over nothing other than air, and apart from a few Ether Deposits, it only leads to the main entrance to the Ether Mine, Drainage Outlet. There is, however, an Ether Planter here, on one of the smaller paths which leads into the cliff. After Mechonis Core, the previous normal enemies of the area are all replaced by Telethia, except for the Water Upa and Graceful Holand that still appear only during rain.
Steady Cuisses are heavy legs armour in . They can be dropped by Leg Arduns.
Steady Greaves are heavy feet armour in . They can be dropped by Beach Krabbles and Cute Brogs.
Stellar Gear (Japanese: , Sutera Gia) is medium head armour in and . They are enhanced versions of the High Entia army's helmets.
Stellar Armour is medium torso armour in and . It is commonly worn by soldiers in the High Entia army.

Stone Krabbles (Japanese: , Sutōn Kuraibu) are enemies in . They are members of the Krabble family, and can be found at level 6-9 along Hazzai Cape and south of Agora Shore in Colony 9. Two of them must be defeated to complete Colony 9's Monster Quest 2 - Part 3, and can drop Small Shells, which are required for Material Quest 1.
Stellar Gauntlets are medium arms armour in and . They are commonly worn by members of the High Entia army.
Stellar Leggings are medium legs armour in and . They can be dropped by various Mechon in Sword Valley and Galahad Fortress. They are enhanced versions of High Entia army greaves.

The Spring of Grief (Japanese: , Nageki no Izumi) is a landmark in . It is located in Tephra Cave, by the central lake in Tephra Cavern. It is the location of the Solid Konev and a Heart-to-Heart - "Glowing in the Night" - as well as being passed through immediately before a mini-boss fight with multiple Arachno.
Stellar Boots are medium feet armour in and . They are commonly worn by High Entia troops.
Strike Biter (Japanese: , Ichigeki no Kamukamu) is a Weapon used by Riki in . It can be dropped by many Armus in Colony 9, or Mount Torta in Bionis' Leg.
Storm Shots (Japanese: , Sutōmushotto) are weapons in . They are ether rifles wielded by Sharla.

Stop the Mechon Rampage! (Japanese: , Kishinhei Tairyō Tōbatsu) is a quest in . This quest can be received from Eleqa after completing Protect the Village. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment.
Strike Lance Sildras (Japanese: , Shōtotsu Kaseyari Shirudora) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are gunlances wielded by Reyn.
Steel Katanas (Japanese: , Zantetsutō, Steel-cutting Sword) are weapons in . They are swords wielded by Dunban.
Spirit Rifle (Japanese: , Supirittoraifuru) is an Ether Rifle in that can be wielded by Sharla. It can be purchased at the Zokhed Pass Shop and Colony 6 Shop 5 for 19,200 G
Spit Clusters (Japanese: , Supittokurasutā) are weapons in . They are ether rifles wielded by Sharla.

The Statue Summit (Japanese: , Shimai-zō Saijōbu) is a landmark in . It is located in Satorl Marsh, at the top of the Sororal Statues, and can only be reached by climbing up them. There is an entrance here which leads into the Terminal Trachea of Bionis' Interior.

The Statue Water is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is required for Preparing for Adventure, and can be found under the small waterfall to the northeast of the Sororal Statues landmark in Satorl Marsh.

Splendid Botis (Japanese: , Meiō no Botisu) is a Unique Monster in . It can be found at level 58 on the Digit 5 Beach, east of the Black Wreckage on the Fallen Arm. It takes the appearance of an Offensive Security Unit.
Steel Strike (Japanese: , Tekkōdan) is one of Dunban's physical arts in . It inflicts Topple to a target when hit and if the target is debuffed with Break.

Sticky Web Fibres are rare materials in . They can be dropped by Leg Arachnos on Bionis' Leg, and traded for in Colony 9 and the Refugee Camp. According to their description, they are gummy threads and sticking them on the soles of the shoes keeps standing. Three are needed for Being a Good Grandfather.
Spirit Breath (Japanese: , Kamui Ibuki) is one of Dunban's arts in . Upon activation, this aura clears his debuffs and grants Haste. The aura's colour is translucent green.

The Starlight Book is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a book of Giant legends. Obtaining it is the objective of The Book of Bafalgar. It can be found by going south from Bafalgar Tomb and taking the south exit of the crossroad onto an elevated ledge above the Vilia Lake area. The item is on the eastern end of the ledge.

Storm Vangs (Japanese: , Sutōmu Vanpu) are enemies in . They are members of the Vang family, and can be found at level 26-27 in the Basin Cave in Satorl Marsh. They can drop the Vang Milk Teeth needed for Let's Make Fillings!.

The Statue Fragment is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is found on the western statue near the Sororal Statues landmark, and can be reached by dropping from the Ether deposit at the statue's neck or from the small platform behind the statue's shoulder. It is required for Cursed Berryjammy but is not exclusive to this quest.

Spirit - Mumkhar (Japanese: , Shinentai Mumuka) is a story exclusive enemy in . It is a Spirit and it can be fought at level 79 near Saturn in Memory Space. Spirit - Mumkhar appears as a translucent green version of Metal Face. It is a minor enemy, and thus fighting it is optional. Like all enemies in Memory Space, Spirit - Mumkhar drops no treasure chests and carries no items which can be stolen. ※ Spirit - Mumkhar will respawn after some time, but Memory Space cannot be visited during normal gameplay.

Spirit - Xord (Japanese: , Shinentai Zōdo) is a story exclusive enemy in . It is a Spirit that can be fought at level 78 near Jupiter in Memory Space. Spirit - Xord appears as a translucent green version of Xord. It is a minor enemy, and thus fighting it is optional. Like all enemies in Memory Space, Spirit - Xord drops no treasure chests and carries no items which can be stolen. ※ Spirit - Xord will respawn after some time, but Memory Space cannot be visited during normal gameplay.

Spirit - Telethia (Japanese: , Shinentai Tereshia) is a story exclusive enemy in . It is a Spirit that can be fought at level 80 near Mars in Memory Space. Spirit - Telethia appears as a translucent green version of a Sani Telethia. It is a minor enemy, and thus fighting it is optional. Like all enemies in Memory Space, Spirit - Telethia drops no treasure chests and carries no items which can be stolen. ※ Spirit - Telethia will respawn after some time, but Memory Space cannot be visited during normal gameplay.

Story Quests are quests that are encountered naturally as a part of the progression of the plot of and . They operate in all the same ways as any other quest, except that the story will not progress until they are completed. There are 31 Story Quests in and 2 Story Quests in . Unlike most other types of quests, Story Quests do not award the player when completing them.

Spirits (Japanese: , Shinentai, Thought Form) are a particular enemy "species" in . They are all sight story exclusive enemies. They are only found in Memory Space near the end of the game, leading up to the final battle with Zanza. There are only four known Spirits. Since most spirits, especially Spirit - Xord, do not have many arts, they will not use arts often because of the cooldown times.

The Storage Depot (Japanese: , Shizai Okiba) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of the Ether Mine and is found by travelling south from Test Pit 3. It is here that the party discovers Otharon defending himself against a small group of Mechon. The party defeats the Mechon, and Otharon then leads the party to the Mining Base to recount his and Gadolt's last attempt to reclaim Colony 6.

The Steel Claws (Japanese: , Kōtetsu Tsume) are a unique weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mumkhar's weapon, and cannot be removed from him nor used outside of the time he is in the party. Its gem is Unbeatable VI with a 100% value.

Storage Probes are types of Data Probes in . They increase the amount of Miranium that can be preserved and stored by 3000 units, but only generate mining and revenue at 10% efficiency. Storage probes exist only in a single grade, and linking them will boost their effectiveness. However, greater gains can be obtained by placing them next to Duplicator Probes or Booster Probes.

Stone Potamuses (Japanese: , Sutōn Hippo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Potamus family, and can be found at level 2 in Starfall Basin and level 7-8 near a watering hole north of Shadow Rise in Primordia.
Starlight Duster is one of Doug's two Signature Arts in . Cross learns this Art after completing Close Comrades.

Stickstone Rise (Japanese: , Sutekkirokku no Oka) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the northwest part of Primordia, southwest of FN Site 105 and northwest of Greater Gemini Bridge.
Stella (Japanese: , Sutera) is a Human in . She can be found at the BLADE Tower in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. She is a BLADE officer.
Stoyanov Trail (Japanese: , Irian Toreiru, Irian Trail) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in southwestern Oblivia, northwest of Mesa Fortress.

Stealth Tectinsulas (Japanese: , Suterusu Tapenta) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Tectinsula family and can be found at level 46-47 near the Decapotamon in Noctilum, mostly camouflaged in the ground as hidden enemies.

Steel Suids (Japanese: , Suchīru Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found at level 26-28 on Primordia's Talon Rock Second Terrane. They can drop the Suid Fillet needed for Suid Sirloin.

Steel Femina Suids (Japanese: , Suchīru Femina Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found at level 26-28 on Primordia's Talon Rock Second Terrane.
Sprinter is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is triggered when a character sprints for at least three seconds during a battle.

Stray Mephites (Japanese: , Sutorei Mepitesu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Mephite family, and can be found at level 21-22 near FN Site 312 in Oblivia. Six of them must be defeated to complete the Basic Mission Mephite Mayhem.
Strange Vespers (Japanese: , Sutorenji Usuperu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Vesper family, and can be found at level 18-20 in the Devil's Colony in Oblivia.
Storm Caro (Japanese: , Sutōmu Nokkusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Caro family and can be found at level 51 at the Cauldros Threshold in Sylvalum at night.

Strike Pugiliths (Japanese: , Atakku Berudero) are two Story and Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Pugilith machines, Ganglion's vehicles, and can be found at level 28 at the NLA Primary Defense Line in Primordia during Chapter 8. Two of them must be defeated in the first wave of Ganglion attacks.

Strange Murras (Japanese: , Sutorenji Tondomu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Murra family, and can be found at level 42-44 in Sylvalum, near FN Site 404 or FN Site 410.

Spy Games (Japanese: , Sakudō, Machinations) is an Affinity Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received in front of BLADE Tower in New Los Angeles. It is required to be completed, prior to starting Chapter 9.
Starfall Rondo is one of many Melee Arts in . It can be learned by Blast Fencers like Doug and Yelv.

Spring Unafulges (Japanese: , Supuringu Purumō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Unafulge family, and can be found at level 11-20 in the Whale's Nostril in Noctilum. Five must be defeated during Arms Testers Wanted.

Storm Jaculs (Japanese: , Sutōmu Hasutara) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Jacul family, and can be found at level 41-43 at Emerian Battlegrounds and eastern Mount M'gando and level 46-49 on the walkways north of Mount M'gando in Cauldros.
Sports Complex (Japanese: , Supōtsu Sukuea, Sports Square) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the Residential District of New Los Angeles.
The Starboard (Japanese: , Ugen) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the Ma-non Ship of New Los Angeles.

Stagnant Grexes (Japanese: , Ritādo Rupusu, Retard Lupus) are five Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Grex family, and can be found at level 20-21 at Grieving Plains in Primordia. Defeating them is required during the Normal Mission Water Woes.

Stagnant Terebras (Japanese: , Ritādo Rutoru) are five Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Terebra family, and can be found at level 21 – 23 at Biahno Lake in Primordia. Defeating them is required during the Normal Mission Water Woes.
Staccata (Japanese: , Sutakatta) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Cathedral in the Residential District of New Los Angeles at night.
Stretching Locusts (Japanese: , Shinshuku Batta) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, in particular at Sickle Rock Rise.
Steel Tail Sheaths (Japanese: , Sōden no Kōbishō) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular near FN Site 322.
Strawlennies (English dub: , Japanese: , Sutororenī) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia.
Starlight Apples (Japanese: , Sutappuru) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, on the Grieving Plains and at FN Site 104.
Straw Buoys (Japanese: , Chijimi Ukiwa) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.
Spore Balloons (Japanese: , Hōshi Fūsen) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.
Stargazers (Japanese: , Hoshimi no Chōtō) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.

Spirit Wands (Japanese: , Shōryō no Eda) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum, in particular at FN Site 409 and near Shivering Sands, at the FN Sites 401 and 402, or west of them on the Sylvalum Waters. Gathering one is required during Professor B's Return.
Stone Screws (Japanese: , Sukuryū Rokku) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.
Starmakers (Japanese: , Sutāmeikā) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum, in particular on Needle Rock Sandsea. Five are needed for Nopon Chest.
Stone Lenses (Japanese: , Ishirenzu) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros.
Standard Cranks are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Puges.

Squall Blattas (Japanese: , Sukōru Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family. They can be found at level 60 in Noctilum, within the giant flower in the Divine Roost.

The Stonelattice Cavern (Japanese: , Gankōshi no Dōkutsu) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia. It is filled with lava and Petramands, and contains several lattice-like stone walkways that give the cavern its name. It can be reached on foot by going to FN Site 101, jumping off the cliff to the north (where black smokes can be viewed) and examining the cliff about halfway down.

The Strike Satellis (Japanese: , Atakku Sateresu) is a Main Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is fought at level 47 at Lifehold Core's Interior during Chapter 12. It assists the Vita during the second round. This boss and the other Satellises are not registered in the Enemy Index, only the Vita and the Sentinel Satellis will be registered.
Stola, the Champion (, Yūsha Sutora) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Liceor family. It can be found at level 57 at Seabird's Beak in Sylvalum during crimson auroras.

Stola, the Unchained (, Kakusei no Sutora) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Liceor family. It can be found at level 57 at Delusians South Summit in Sylvalum during rising energy mist, surrounded by four Divine Liceors. It replaces the Dazzling Liceor normally found there. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Stola, the Unchained.

Stray Ovis (Japanese: , Sutorei Owisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Ovis family, and can be found at level 44 at Vitriol Cesspool in Noctilum when summoned by Lugalbanda, the Wanderer-King, whom they assist. They do not drop any materials, and vanish when Lugalbanda is defeated.

Strange Saltats (Japanese: , Sutorenji Sarutāto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Saltat family, and can be found at level 31-40 at Scholes Battlegrounds in Cauldros during clear weather.

Strange Liceors (Japanese: , Sutorenji Kurāra) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Liceor family, and can be found at level 16-19 at Needle Rock Sandsea and the Southern Searoad in Sylvalum. Three must be defeated to complete Bottoms Up. They drop Giant Blue Pearls, two of which are needed for the mission The Jewelmonger.

Stalker Blattas (Japanese: , Sutōku Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 21-30 in Primordia, north of FN Site 112 or southwest of FN Site 113 during the day.

Stalwart Blattas (Japanese: , Sutādi Buratta, Sturdy Blatta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 21-30 in Noctilum, near FN Site 216, in Decapotamon.

Statue Scintimures (Japanese: , Sutachū Torizumo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Scintimure family, and can be found at level 58 in the Cavernous Abyss, at level 55 at Anvil Sandplain, and at level 52-59 in Behemoth's Shadows in Sylvalum.

Spore Filiavents (Japanese: , Supoa Nagwada) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X and are members of the Filiavent family. One can be found at level 51-60 at Ensanguined Font in Noctilum at night.
Standard Blade Modules are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from red Shrads in Cauldros. Five are required for the affinity mission What the Skell?!.

The Stout Caro (Japanese: , Sutauto Nokkusu) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Caro family. It is fought at level 33 at Sandsprint Slope in Sylvalum during the Affinity Mission Soldier of the Harriers.
Steady Hand is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Commando at rank 3. Cross, Elma, Phog, and Celica can use this skill.
Steel Flesh is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Striker at rank 2. Cross, Lin, L, H.B., Alexa and Nagi can use this skill.
Stand Strong is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Shield Trooper at rank 10. Cross, Lin and L can use this skill.
Stellar Entry is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Galactic Knight at rank 9.

The Stratospheric Balaena (Japanese: , Sutorato Baraena) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in . It is a member of the Balaena family. It is found at level 46 the Floating Reef in Oblivia only during Fitting In. It drops no treasure.

Stainless Fal-swos (Japanese: , Suten Gi-suo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Fal-swo machines, and can be found at level 34 at Needle Rock Sandsea and at level 39 at South Silent Sandsea in Sylvalum during the night.
Squashing Scirpos is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Pathfinders and the primary destination is Noctilum.
Standard Jammers are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Quos.
Standard Sensor Parts are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Zigs.
Strike Gunner Zigs (Japanese: , Atakkukyanon Jigu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Zig machines, and can be found at level 41-50 in Cauldros, near FN Site 511.
Strike Launcher Zigs (Japanese: , Atakkuranchā Jigu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Zig machines, and can be found at level 51-60 in Cauldros's Kitsune Stronghold.
Strike Launcher! is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located south of Deliverance Park in the Residential District of New Los Angeles between Alexa and Cross at any time.

Stop, Thief! (Japanese: , Sennyūkan to Henken, Preconception and Prejudice) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Shiraton in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles.
Stout Purgovent Extracts are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from dark-colored Purgovents in Sylvalum.
Steel Unafulge Cells are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Unafulges.
Straight from the Heart is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a female BLADE and the primary destination is Oblivia.
Standing Tall(er) is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Nopon Commerce Guild and the primary destination is Oblivia.

Strike Puges (Japanese: , Atakku Berude) are Story Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Puge machines, Ganglion's human size robots, and can be found at level 26 in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles during Chapter 8 when the Ganglion attack.
Standard Coils are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Oc-servs.
Sticky Scirpo Silks are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Scirpos.
Standard Shafts are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from most Zigs.

Storms and Heat is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.2, and is unlocked if the Scintimure is defeated during Leadership Strike. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Stolen Skell Smashdown is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.9, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting eight Ictuses. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Squad Tasks were an online gameplay mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They were one of the two components of BLADE Missions. By completing them, players could earn Reward Tickets and BLADE Medals, as well as access the corresponding Squad Missions. This mechanic was discontinued with the shutdown of Wii U online servicess. During normal gameplay, a BLADE Mission may be randomly assigned to the player's Squad. A Squad Task panel appeared in the lower right of the screen, and the player could decide whether or not to participate in the BLADE Mission. Squad Missions were an online gameplay mechanic in . They were one of the two components of BLADE Missions. By completing them, players could earn Credits, Experience Points, Reward Tickets, and Battle Points. The mechanic was discontinued following the shutdown of Wii U online services, but it was restored for the Definitive Edition for the Nintendo Switch, which requires the purchase of a Nintendo Switch Online pass. The Stray Potamus (Japanese: , Sutorei Hippo) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Potamus and can be found at level 25 in Sylvalum on the southern part of the strip of land separating the two halves of Lake Ciel. It drops the Sapphire Ring needed to start Hair Apparent. When Hair Apparent is completed, the Stray Potamus will respawn, but if it is defeated again it will drop a second Sapphire Ring and not respawn.
